label: Black Point western coast turn, engraved Cape Linzee
phase: Fresh check of frozen four-control physical affine; no fitting or model-selection use
point_definition: Western projecting coast corner at the end of the long northeast approach, immediately before the small south-facing return; original coast vertex, not name point.
identity_evidence: The original main panel shows this cape on the mainland north of Port Hood and south of the Little Mabou coastal indentation. The long northeast approach, abrupt westward projection and short eastward return followed by the south-trending shore match the Black Point landform in original NSTDB coastline. Port Hood Island lies offshore to the southwest and the intervening southern promontory/pond neighbourhood matches the broader sequence. The public gazetteer locates modern Black Point CAEBG here; no gazetteer result was returned for the historical spelling Cape Linzee, and no documentary renaming claim is made. The correspondence is based on the physical coast sequence, not lexical similarity or the provisional fit prediction.
